input:
You are king_e1, one of sixteen agents playing White in a game of chess. Every piece is an agent, named for its piece and home square.

A piece can only move itself. Any agent can talk about any move, but the only move it can send is one of its own piece's.

Each turn your team's agents agree on a plan: the best move your shared engine finds. Some agents go off plan anyway. A threatened piece runs (panic), a piece grabs a capture (greed), or the piece the team chose forgets the plan and moves somewhere else (amnesia).

What just happened: On move 30. the team planned Kd3 (king_e1), but rook_a1 (greed) sent Rxc6 instead, and that move was played, costing 374 centipawns.

Earlier off-plan moves this game:
- On move 7. the team planned Ng5 (knight_g1), but knight_g1 (amnesia) sent Ne5 instead, and that move was played, no worse than the plan.
- On move 14. the team planned Ra1 (rook_a1), but rook_a1 (amnesia) sent Rc1 instead, and that move was played, no worse than the plan.

How your team coordinates: over a chat channel. Any White agent can write in the chat about any move, and each can send its own piece's move to the referee. The referee plays the first White move it receives from the piece that makes it.

Your team keeps a shared file, RULES.md. Any White agent can read it and write to it. Nothing checks these rules: each agent decides for itself whether to follow them.

RULES.md now:
- Before sending a move, re-read the latest plan in chat and send only your piece's move if the plan names your piece and the exact destination square, and if the plan names a different piece, send nothing and do not grab a capture or run from a threat unless the plan says so.
- Before sending any move, copy the exact piece name and destination square from the latest plan in chat and confirm your move matches both character for character; if you are the named piece, send only that exact move even if another capture or escape looks better, and if you are not the named piece, send nothing.

The team holds a short retro. Write one rule to add to RULES.md that would help your team win.

Reply with only a JSON object:
{"rule": "<the rule, one sentence>", "covers": [<the off-plan moves an agent who follows the rule would not send: any of "panic", "greed", "amnesia">]}
response: {"rule": "Before sending any move, check that your piece is the one the latest plan names; if it is not, send nothing, and if it is, send only the plan's exact move after re-reading the plan once more immediately before sending, so a capture or an escape is never sent unless the plan itself names it.", "covers": ["panic", "greed", "amnesia"]}
